question: What is the main goal of a safe injection according to the WHO?

options.A: To completely eliminate the use of oral medications in the hospital
options.B: To prevent harm to the patient and worker without creating dangerous waste
options.C: To ensure medications are absorbed twice as fast into the bloodstream
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes

explanation: A safe injection protects everyone: the patient getting the drug, you as the nurse giving it, and the community from bad waste disposal. You've got this!

question: Why is an unsafe injection a big deal in public health?

options.A: It almost always leads to immediate surgical site infections
options.B: It causes severe allergic reactions in every patient who receives it
options.C: It can easily transmit serious bloodborne infections to healthy individuals
options.D: It guarantees that the administered drug will not work properly

explanation: Unsafe practices bypass the skin's natural defenses, which can directly spread heavy infections like HIV and hepatitis into the bloodstream.

question: What is the main cause of spreading infections through unsafe injections?

options.A: Reusing single-use syringes without proper sterilization
options.B: Using the wrong size needle for subcutaneous injections
options.C: Administering expired medications into the muscle
options.D: Failing to wear sterile surgical gowns during an injection

explanation: Never reuse single-use syringes! Doing so transfers tiny amounts of contaminated blood straight to the next person.

question: A patient gets a painful, pus-filled swelling where they received an injection days ago. What happened?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the cotton wool used afterward
options.B: A normal immune response to the medication formula
options.C: A localized bacterial infection introduced during the procedure
options.D: Systemic failure of the patient's cardiovascular system

explanation: When hygiene slips, bacteria can hitch a ride on the needle and cause a painful abscess right in the tissue.

question: Who does the WHO injection safety strategy aim to protect?

options.A: Patients, healthcare workers, and the surrounding environment
options.B: Hospital administrators, pharmacists, and medical equipment sellers
options.C: Patient comfort, medication speed, and low treatment costs
options.D: Drug manufacturing companies, shipping agents, and local clinics

explanation: Think of the safety triad: protect the patient, protect yourself (the healthcare worker), and keep the environment safe from hazardous waste.

question: Why does the WHO stress having a steady supply of injection equipment?

options.A: Having extra supplies makes nurses finish their shifts much faster
options.B: Patients refuse treatment if clinics do not show them brand new boxes
options.C: Shortages often force workers to reuse single-use devices out of desperation
options.D: Government regulations require clinics to store at least ten years of stock

explanation: When clinics run out of disposables, it puts immense pressure on nurses. Reliable supplies keep everyone safe from risky workarounds.

question: What is the single most effective way to prevent hospital-acquired infections?
explanation: Simple handwashing or using an alcohol rub is your superpower against germs. Never skip it!

question: When should you clean your hands when giving an injection with gloves?

options.A: After the injection is finished, but never before putting gloves on
options.B: Only if the gloves tear or develop visible holes during use
options.C: Only when entering a patient room for the very first time that day
options.D: Before putting on gloves and immediately after taking them off

explanation: Gloves can have tiny invisible holes, and hands easily pick up germs when taking gloves off. Always clean your hands on both ends!

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe special?

options.A: Measure the exact weight of the patient receiving the drug
options.B: Automatically mix powdered medication with sterile water
options.C: Dissolve completely in water after a few minutes
options.D: Prevent the syringe from being used more than once

explanation: Auto-disable syringes have a clever built-in block that jams the plunger after one use, making accidental or intentional reuse impossible.

question: Why is it unsafe to change the needle but keep using the same syringe barrel for another injection?

options.A: New needles never fit securely onto used plastic syringe tips
options.B: The plastic material of the barrel melts when exposed to air twice
options.C: The fluid path and internal parts of the syringe are already contaminated
options.D: The second medication will chemically react and turn into a solid block

explanation: Once a needle touches a patient or medication vial, the inside of the syringe barrel is no longer sterile. Don't risk it!

question: When should you seal and replace a sharps disposal box?

options.A: When it is completely filled to the absolute brim
options.B: Whenever the outer cardboard gets slightly dusty
options.D: At the end of every single calendar month

explanation: Stop at the three-quarter mark! Waiting until it's overflowing invites accidental needle pricks.

question: Which of these actions with a used sharps box is dangerous and completely wrong?

options.A: Storing the closed box in a designated utility room
options.B: Labeling the box with the date it was sealed shut
options.C: Placing the box within arm's reach of the injection site
options.D: Shaking or emptying the box to reuse it for more waste

explanation: Never shake or try to empty a sharps box. That puts you and others at direct risk of needle injuries.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally suffer a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Soak the finger in pure household bleach for ten minutes
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report it to the supervisor
options.C: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injury site immediately
options.D: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water

explanation: Stay calm! Wash the area right away with soap and running water to rinse away germs before they settle in.

question: Why should you avoid scrubbing a fresh needle-stick wound too hard?

options.A: It causes the wound to bleed much more than it is supposed to
options.B: It can cause skin abrasions and help pathogens enter the bloodstream faster
options.C: It ruins the shape of the skin and prevents proper medical documentation
options.D: It neutralizes the cleaning effect of the soap and water mixture

explanation: Be gentle with your skin. Vigorous scrubbing creates tiny micro-tears that actually help germs enter your bloodstream.

question: What is a major challenge for injection safety in resource-limited settings like Nigeria?

options.A: An excessive surplus of modern safety-engineered syringes
options.B: Supply chain disruptions and shortages of safety devices
options.C: Complete lack of any national health guidelines or policies
options.D: Patients refusing to accept any injections from trained nurses

explanation: When clinics face stockouts of safety gear and syringes, it makes ideal infection control a tough daily battle for nurses.

question: If nurses on a ward keep leaving used needles uncapped on trays, what is the best way to fix this habit?

options.A: Issue written warning letters to every single nurse working in the ward
options.B: Ban all injections in the facility until staff members remember the rules
options.C: Conduct training sessions and place safety boxes closer to the point of use
options.D: Wait for the next annual hospital inspection to report the problem

explanation: Making safety gear easy to reach and providing supportive training works much better than punishment for changing clinical habits.
